title: Automatiqa disclosure envelope
description: Machine-readable marking of AI-generated content, per EU AI Act Art. 50(2). The same five facts are expressed in whatever each output format allows: a JSON field, an HTML meta tag, YAML front matter, a PDF info dictionary and XMP packet, PPTX core properties, or a PNG text chunk.

value.description: True when any model-generated content is present. Emit the envelope only when true - absence of the envelope means no AI-generated content, which must stay a truthful statement.

scope.description: Which parts the model wrote, in the product's own vocabulary. Examples: ["summary"], ["article_summaries", "executive_summary"], ["canvas_items"]. Never the whole document when only parts are generated.

schema.description: Version of this convention. Consumers key idempotency off this field, so marking twice is a no-op.

system.description: The product that produced the output, e.g. "procezio" or "ops-risk-monitor".

review_state.description: Whether a human accepted the generated content before it left the system. "none" where the product has no review step.

items_drafted.description: Count of model-written items, where the product has a countable unit.

items_total.description: Total items, so a reader can weigh how much of the artefact is generated.

model.description: Optional and off by default. Art. 50 never requires naming the model. Set it only where the operator chose the model themselves and provenance aids incident investigation; never where the endpoint is the end user's own, since printing it leaks their local setup.

ts.description: When the output was produced, RFC 3339.
